title: Patch channel strategy and signature workflow for private deployments
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working playbook for how we manage patch channels, image signing, and release orchestration for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. The intention is to define a low-friction flow for: small security patches, critical fixes, and scheduled feature rollouts while preserving reproducible provenance and fast rollback. This doc focuses on interactions between Terraform modules, the GitOps operator (Argo/Flux style assumptions), Helm chart boundaries, and image signing/attestation (cosign + KMS).

Principles we keep: 
- Safe by default: any release path MUST allow automated rollback or a fast backout.
- Signed provenance: every promoted artifact must be cryptographically verifiable and tied to CI metadata.
- Channel semantics: channels indicate risk/urgency (patch, stable, canary, manual-preview).
- Minimal blast radius: channels map to Kubernetes namespaces and traffic routing policies when possible.
- Reproducible infra: Terraform modules define operator contract and CI hooks; changes to TF must be reviewed with release owners.

Channel definitions (simple):
- patch: emergency or security-only. Single-cluster impact; auto-rollback policy aggressive (5–10 min monitoring buffer).
- stable: default production channel; batch of changes tested in staging.
- canary: small % of traffic or single node pool; longer observation window, automatic progressive rollout if checks pass.
- preview: ephemeral environment per PR or release candidate. Manual promotion only.

High-level flow (CI -> Signing -> Promotion -> GitOps -> Operator):
1) CI produces container image + SBOM + provenance JSON; pushes to internal registry with CI build id tag.
2) Sign image: CI calls cosign using customer-specific KMS key (or central Redwood signing key when customer allows). Signature and attestation are uploaded alongside image; attestations include git commit, build id, TF plan checksum, chart digest.
3) Attach release metadata to artifact repo: channel label (initially preview or canary), terraform-module-checksum, helm-chart-checksum.
4) Promotion job (manual or automated) mutates the GitOps repo: for patch channel, create a patch manifest (kustomize overlay) targeting patch-namespace or production annotation depending on customer policy. For stable, update Helm values in production overlay.
5) Argo/Flux detects change and applies. The operator validates image signature before admission (mutating/admission webhook + operator-level verification).
6) Post-deploy monitors run smoke checks; automatic rollback triggered on SLO breaches or failed checks per policy.

Terraform module notes (operator & channel wiring):
- module.private_operator
  - exposes: argocd_app_repo (git url), chart_location, allowed_channels (list), signature_key_ref (kms key id), admission_webhook_enabled (bool)
  - outputs used by CI: argocd_app_path, helm_release_name
  - Add a tfvar: release_channel_default to bootstrap small customers on stable or canary.
- module.registry_access
  - provides signed-registry-pull-secret and attestation-verifier-rolebindings.
  - make the cosign verifier image configurable; default to our hardened verifier image.
- module.networking
  - channels should map to dedicated Service subsets or node pools via labels; expose an optional patch-isolation boolean to create temporary NetworkPolicy objects during emergency patches.

Helm chart and overlay conventions:
- Chart metadata must include an annotations block for "artifact.provenance" with build id and digest.
- Value patterns: image.tag must be explicit immutable tag; never use :latest for any channel.
- Provide a small hooks folder: pre-deploy-sanity, post-deploy-smoke, and rollback-hooks that execute against the operator API (use lightweight sidecar jobs).
- Patch overlay generator: a simple kustomize/ytt template used by promotion job to produce minimum diff (app label + image.tag + annotation changes). Keep this under the GitOps repo in /overlays/patches/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<ticket>.

Image signing and KMS behavior (practical):
- Signing flows: CI job signs artifacts with cosign using either customer KMS key (preferred) or CI-signed key. Key selection is driven by a terraform secret ref.
- Attestations: include SBOM (CycloneDX), build logs link, TF plan artifact checksum, and CI run id. Store attestations in registry and push a copy to internal artifact store (retention policy 180 days).
- Verification: operator's webhook verifies signature and checks that the attestation channel label matches the GitOps change. If mismatch, reject and create an incident comment in the PR.

Rollout & rollback policies (defaults we recommend):
- Patch channel: 1 node pool / 1% traffic, health window 10m with 2 consecutive check failures trigger rollback.
- Canary: progressive rollout 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 15m observations each step. Auto-failback to previous stable after N failures.
- Stable: manual promotion from canary, post-deploy smoke of 30m before marking as release.

Preflight checks (local & CI):
- Terraform plan guard: CI must include terraform plan upload; promotion is blocked if plan diff touches module.private_operator.signature_key_ref without review.
- Helm lint + templated values must pass in CI.
- SBOM and cosign signature existence enforced by gate job.
- Operator compatibility: run a short e2e in ephemeral preview (k8s kind) before promotion to canary.

Operational runbook (abridged):
- Emergency patch start: create patch branch in gitops repo with overlay, include ticket id and signed artifact tag. Open PR to ops team.
- Apply patch: ops lead triggers promotion pipeline which updates repo. Argo applies automatically.
- Monitor: use the smoke dashboard (per-channel) and slack alerts to #ops-private. If errors exceed threshold, initiate rollback via helper script that reverts commit and re-signs older tag for operator validation.
- Postmortem: fill template linked to JIRA and include artifact provenance as evidence.

Open items / TODOs:
- Define a tidy format for the TF plan checksum attestation and where it's stored. (Marta to draft schema)
- Small script to auto-generate patch overlays to reduce human error (spike by Q1 2025).
- Add documented interface for customers who want to opt-out of internal cosign, including consent forms and KMS onboarding checklist.
- Flesh out operator admission webhook failure modes and clear user-facing error messages.

References / links used during drafting:
- GH: private-deploy-operator (PRs and issues) - see linked artifacts
- JIRA-OPS-778: small-patch-flow-proposal
- Internal runbooks: confluence://runbooks/private-deploys/patches (placeholder)

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally pragmatic and leans on operator-side verification. Feedback especially wanted on: label->channel mapping, TF module surface area (are we leaking too much), and cosign key lifecycle operational burden.
